record.title: Local short-generator conjecture for expanders of ${\rm PSL}_2({\mathbb F}_p)$
record.statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $\Sigma_p$ satisfy

$$
\langle \Sigma_p\rangle={\rm PSL}_2({\mathbb F}_p).
$$

**Local short-generator conjecture.** There is a constant $C$, independent of $p$, such that the ball of radius $C$ in the generating set $\Sigma_p$ contains two elements $g,h$ with

$$
\operatorname{girth}\bigl(\mathcal{G}({\rm PSL}_2({\mathbb F}_p),\{g,h\})\bigr)\geq \frac{1}{C}\log p.
$$

Combined with the cited expansion result, this would imply that Cayley graphs of ${\rm SL}_2({\mathbb F}_p)$ are expanders for every choice of generators. The paper provides no resolution.
record.source_name: Alex Gamburd, Shlomo Hoory, Mehrdad Shahshahani, Aner Shalev and Balint Virag, “On the girth of random Cayley graphs”, arXiv:0707.1833 (2007).

record.title: The generalized Bunkbed conjecture for two-color edge percolation
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, let $T\subseteq V(G)$, and let $\tilde G=G\times K_2$. In the model $E_3^T(\tilde G)$, every horizontal edge is assigned independently to the downstairs or upstairs layer with equal probability, and vertical edges are present exactly at vertices in $T$. Equivalently, color every edge of $G$ red or blue independently with equal probability; a walk may change color only at a vertex of $T$.

**Two-color Bunkbed conjecture.** For every $u,v\in V(G)$,

$$
P(u_0\longleftrightarrow v_0)\ge P(u_0\longleftrightarrow v_1).
$$

This is a stronger-looking reformulation of the conditioned model and is proved in the paper for some graph classes. Its validity for arbitrary graphs and arbitrary $T$ remains open.
record.source_name: Svante Linusson, “On percolation and the bunkbed conjecture”, arXiv:0811.0949 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0949

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2008).

record.title: The combinatorial Sylvester four-point conjecture
record.statement:
Fix $n\geq 4$. Let $\mathsf{w}$ be a uniformly random reduced expression for the long word in $S_n$, and choose uniformly at random a $4$-subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The induced reduced expression $\mathsf{v}$ for the long word in $S_4$ is compared with

$$
X=\{s_1s_2s_3s_2s_1s_2,\ s_3s_2s_1s_2s_3s_2,\ s_2s_1s_2s_3s_2s_1,\ s_2s_3s_2s_1s_2s_3\}.
$$

**Combinatorial Sylvester four-point conjecture.** For every $n\geq 4$, the probability that $\mathsf{v}\in X$ is $1/4$.

This is a combinatorial analogue of Sylvester's four-point problem, obtained from the Goodman–Pollack classification of point configurations. A more general result of O. Angel and A. E. Holroyd is stated to imply this conjecture.
record.source_name: Gregory S. Warrington, “A combinatorial version of Sylvester's four-point problem”, arXiv:0910.5945 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5945

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2009).

record.title: A four-point multiplicative configuration conjecture in finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $S\subset G\times G$. For a fixed density parameter $\delta>0$, consider sets satisfying $|S|\geq \delta|G|^2$. **Four-point configuration conjecture.** For every $\delta>0$ there is a threshold $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that whenever $|G|\geq n_0$, every set $S\subset G\times G$ with $|S|\geq \delta|G|^2$ contains four elements $(a,b),(a,c),(e,c),(e,f)$ such that

$$
ab=ec\quad\text{and}\quad ac=ef.
$$

This is proposed as a stronger version of the preceding density theorem for finite groups, which guarantees only three elements with the corresponding multiplicative relations. The statement is presented as an unproved strengthening, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Jozsef Solymosi, “Roth type theorems in finite groups”, arXiv:1201.3670 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.3670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

record.title: Regular hypergraph overlapping Hamilton cycle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb H^{(k)}(n,d)$ denote the random $d$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $k>\ell\geq 2$, an **$\ell$-overlapping cycle** is a $k$-uniform hypergraph whose edges arise from a cyclic vertex ordering, with each edge consisting of $k$ consecutive vertices and each pair of consecutive edges sharing exactly $\ell$ vertices. **Overlapping Hamilton cycle conjecture.** For every $k>\ell\geq 2$, if $d\gg n^{\ell-1}$, then

$$
\mathbb H^{(k)}(n,d)\text{ contains an $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton cycle a.a.s.}
$$

Thresholds for $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton cycles in random hypergraphs with independent edges are known, but the analogous result for random regular hypergraphs with arbitrary $\ell\geq 2$ remains open.
record.source_name: Andrzej Dudek, Alan Frieze, Andrzej Ruciński and Matas Šileikis, “Loose Hamilton Cycles in Regular Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1304.1426 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.1426

record.title: The main conjecture on exponential growth of product replacement graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite group generated by $d$ elements. The **main conjecture** asserts that the product replacement graphs $\Gamma_k(G)$ have exponential growth for all $k\ge d+1$. If these graphs are disconnected, this means that at least one connected component has exponential growth. The conjecture is motivated by the relationship between product replacement graphs and Nielsen transformations, and is weaker than the expected non-amenability statement. It is known for several classes of groups, including the Grigorchuk groups studied in the paper, but remains open for general infinite groups.
record.source_name: Anton Malyshev and Igor Pak, “Growth in product replacement graphs”, arXiv:1304.5320 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5320

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2013). “Similarly, in case Conjecture proves too difficult, there is a weaker and perhaps more accessible open problem.”

record.title: The logarithmic bound conjecture for the degree-sequence parameters
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a strict graphic sequence, and for each $1\leq i\leq n$ let $r_i$ be the variable defined in the source. **Logarithmic bound conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\left|\log(r_i)\right|<c\cdot\log(n)
$$

for every $1\leq i\leq n$. The paper explains that bounds on the variables $r_i$ are crucial to its main proof and conjectures that they remain valid for strict graphic sequences in wider generality.
record.source_name: Behzad Mehrdad, “Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence”, arXiv:1401.0220 (2014).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0220

record.title: Conjecture on powers of Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs
record.statement: For $k\geq 2$, let an $(\varepsilon,p,k-1,k)$-pseudorandom graph mean a graph satisfying the stated pseudorandomness condition with parameters $(\varepsilon,p,k-1,k)$. The $k$th power of a Hamilton cycle is obtained by joining every pair of vertices whose distance on the cycle is at most $k$. **Powers-of-Hamilton-cycles conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, the pseudorandomness requirement in Theorem 1 can be replaced by $(\varepsilon,p,k-1,k)$-pseudorandomness. This would extend the result proved in the paper for squared Hamilton cycles to all higher powers, under a weaker pseudorandomness requirement.
record.source_name: Peter Allen, Julia Böttcher, Hiep Hàn, Yury Person and Yoshiharu Kohayakawa, “Powers of Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs”, arXiv:1402.0984 (2014).

record.title: Liu–Wang's log-convexity conjecture for the Eulerian transformation
record.statement: Let $\{x_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ be a sequence of nonnegative numbers, and define $z_n=\sum_{k=0}^n A_{n,k}x_k$ using the Eulerian triangle $\{A_{n,k}\}_{0\leq k\leq n}$. A sequence $\{a_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is **log-convex** if $a_k^2\leq a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$ for every $k\geq 1$. **Liu–Wang's conjecture.** The Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity: whenever $\{x_n\}$ is log-convex, so is $\{z_n\}$. Liu and Wang proposed this conjecture after establishing analogous results for the binomial and Stirling transformations. It is stated in the source as still open.
record.source_name: Lily Li Liu and Bao-Xuan Zhu, “Strong q-log-convexity of the Eulerian polynomials of Coxeter groups”, arXiv:1407.1968 (2014).
record.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2014). “They also proposed the following conjecture, which is still open now.”

record.title: Kikuta–Ruckle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and $d\in(0,1)$. In the KR-Problem, choose nonnegative numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=1$ to maximize the probability that the sum over a uniformly random $k$-element subset exceeds $d$. **Kikuta–Ruckle conjecture.** For every $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and $d\in(0,1)$, there is an optimal solution of the form

$$
a_1=\cdots=a_s=\frac1s,\qquad a_{s+1}=\cdots=a_n=0
$$

for some $s\in\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. The conjecture is described as a central claim for the generalized problem; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Endre Csóka, “Limit theory of discrete mathematics problems”, arXiv:1505.06984 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06984

record.title: Alon's independence-number conjecture for Cayley graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group of odd order $n$, and let $G(\Gamma,T)$ denote the graph associated with a subset $T\subseteq \Gamma$. For a graph $G$, write $\alpha(G)$ for its independence number. **Alon's conjecture.** There exist constants $c_1,c_2$ such that, for every integer $t$ with $1\le t\le n$, there is a subset $T\subseteq \Gamma$ of size $t$ for which

$$
\alpha\bigl(G(\Gamma,T)\bigr)\le c_1\frac{n}{t}(\log n)^{c_2}.
$$

This conjecture asks for sparse Cayley-type graphs with near-optimal independence bounds uniformly over all subset sizes; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Hong Liu and Maryam Sharifzadeh, “The number of subsets of integers with no k-term arithmetic progression”, arXiv:1605.03172 (2016).

record.title: Tightness of the partition-constrained minimization LP for Potts internal energy
record.statement:
Let $d\ge 3$, $q\ge d+1$, and $\beta>0$. Consider the minimization linear program introduced in the paper, whose variables are the probabilities $p_C$ of local views $C$ and whose constraints include the $q$-partition constraints for all $q$-partitions $S$ of size $d$.

**Partition-LP tightness conjecture.** The minimization LP is tight and yields, for every $d$-regular graph $G$,

$$
U^q_{K_{d,d}}(\beta)\le U^q_G(\beta).
$$

The conjecture is based on computations for small values of $d$ at fixed $\beta$ and would establish the lower internal-energy bound from the regular-graph Potts conjecture in the range $d\ge 3$, $q\ge d+1$, $\beta>0$.
record.source_name: Ewan Davies, Matthew Jenssen, Will Perkins and Barnaby Roberts, “Extremes of the internal energy of the Potts model on cubic graphs”, arXiv:1610.08496 (2017).

record.title: Sandpile group distribution conjecture for random directed graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma(n)$ be a sequence of $\epsilon$-balanced random digraphs, and let $S(\Gamma(n))$ denote its total sandpile group. Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and define

$$
Q=\prod_{p\text{ prime}}\prod_{k=2}^{\infty}(1-p^{-k}).
$$

**Sandpile group distribution conjecture.** For every finite abelian group $G$,

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}{\mathbb P}(S(\Gamma(n))=G)=\frac{Q}{|G||\operatorname{Aut}(G)|}.
$$

The preceding results establish convergence for every fixed finite set of prime-primary components, but do not control the entire sandpile group; the conjecture asserts that these restrictions are unnecessary. If true, it would also imply that the probability of being coeulerian converges to $Q$.
record.source_name: Shaked Koplewitz, “Sandpile groups and the coeulerian property for random directed graphs”, arXiv:1611.06444 (2016).

record.title: The high-density $3k-4$ conjecture modulo a prime
record.statement:
Let $G=\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$ with $p\geq 2$ prime, let $A,B\subseteq G$ be nonempty subsets with $A+B\neq G$, and set $C=-G\setminus(A+B)$. Suppose $|A|\geq |B|$ and

$$
|A+B|=|A|+|B|+r\leq \min\{|A|+2|B|-3-\delta_B,\;p-r-3-\delta_C\},
$$

where, for $X\in\{A,B,C\}$ with $(X,Y,Z)$ a permutation of $(A,B,C)$,

$$
\delta_X=\begin{cases}1 & \text{if $r\geq 0$ and $X$ is a translate of either $Y$ or $Z$},\\1 & \text{if $r\geq 2$, $Y$ and $Z$ are translates of each other, and $|Y|=|Z|=r+4$},\\0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

**The high-density $3k-4$ conjecture.** There are arithmetic progressions $P_A,P_B,P_C\subseteq G$, all having a common difference, such that

$$
X\subseteq P_X\quad\text{and}\quad |P_X|\leq |X|+r+1\quad\text{for all $X\in\{A,B,C\}$}.
$$

This conjecture seeks a sharp extension of the integer $3k-4$ theorem to sumsets in $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$ when the sumset and its complement satisfy the stated high-density bounds. The parser supplies no evidence resolving it, so its status is recorded as open.
record.source_name: David J. Grynkiewicz, “The 3k-4 Theorem modulo a Prime: High Density for A+B”, arXiv:2402.15028 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15028

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Paley ETF RIP-constant conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be prime, let $\Phi_p$ be the Paley equiangular tight frame, and let $\delta_K=\delta_K(\Phi_p)$ denote its RIP constant of order $K$. **Paley ETF RIP-constant conjecture.** For every $K\geq 1$,

$$
\delta_K=O\left(\sqrt{\frac{K}{p}}\,\log K\,\log p\right).
$$

Consequently, for constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and $0<\delta<\sqrt{2}-1$, $\Phi_p$ has the $(c_1p/\log^{c_2}p,\delta)$-RIP. The conjecture was proposed as a random-model prediction for Paley ETFs, remains open, and is described as difficult; it is consistent with the conjectured polylogarithmic clique number of Paley graphs.
record.source_name: Shohei Satake, “On the Paley RIP and Paley graph extractor”, arXiv:2405.08608 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1204.5958](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.5958).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.08608

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Boros and Moll's infinite log-concavity conjecture for Boros-Moll sequences
record.statement: Let $d_\ell(m)$ denote the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in the Boros-Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$, for $0\leq \ell\leq m$. A sequence is **$k$-log-concave** when its first $k$ iterates under the operator $\mathcal{L}$ are nonnegative, where $\mathcal{L}(\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0})=\{a_i^2-a_{i-1}a_{i+1}\}_{i\geq 0}$ and $a_{-1}=0$; it is $\infty$-log-concave when this holds for every $k\geq 1$. **Boros and Moll's conjecture.** The Boros-Moll sequence $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{\ell=0}^m$ is $\infty$-log-concave. This conjecture remains open, despite the known log-concavity of these sequences.
record.source_name: James J. Y. Zhao, “The extended reverse ultra log-concavity of transposed Boros-Moll sequences”, arXiv:2406.13790 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: Expected number of draws to obtain a soft streak
record.statement:
Let consecutive letters be drawn uniformly from the alphabet $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and stop when a soft streak of length $k$—that is, a non-decreasing word of length $k$—is obtained. Let $\psi_{k,r}$ and $\omega_k$ be the quantities used in the preceding generating-function identities. Then the expected number of letters drawn is

$$
E_{\mathrm{soft}}(n,k)=\frac{(1-n^{-k})^n}{\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{(k-1)n}\psi_{k,r}\operatorname{B}_s(n,k,r)n^{-r}}
$$

and equivalently

$$
E_{\mathrm{soft}}(n,k)=\frac{k}{\displaystyle\sum_{s=1}^{k-1}(1-\omega_k^{-s})\left(1-\frac{\omega_k^s}{n}\right)^{-n}}.
$$

**Expected-number conjecture.** The expected number of letters drawn is given by these two equivalent expressions.

This is presented as a corollary of the generating-function method and extends the preceding theorem for strictly increasing streaks to soft streaks. The supplied excerpt does not provide evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Senan Sekhon, “Counting words without strictly increasing subwords of fixed length”, arXiv:2511.13287 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Profile conjecture for $S_{2,1}$-good graph sequences
record.statement:
Let $S_{2,1}$ be the relevant colored graph, and let an $S_{2,1}$-good sequence $(G_n)$ have limiting edge density $\beta$ and profile $\rho(S_{2,1},(G_n))$. Define the construction densities $c(\beta)$, $cc(\beta)$, $s(\beta)$, $\ell(\beta)$, and $r(\beta)$ as in the preceding constructions. Let $x\in(0,1)$ solve $cc(x)=c(x)$, equivalently

$$
16x^3-40x^2+41x-16=0,
$$

and let $y\in(0,1/4)$ be a root of the degree-six polynomial determining when the optimum in $s(\beta)$ occurs at $x=0$. **Profile conjecture.** For every $S_{2,1}$-good sequence $(G_n)$,

$$
\left.\begin{array}{ll}cc(\beta)&\text{if }\beta\in[0,x]\\c(\beta)&\text{if }\beta\in[x,1]\end{array}\right\}\leq\rho(S_{2,1},(G_n))\leq\begin{cases}s(\beta)&\text{if }\beta\in[0,y]\\c(\beta)&\text{if }\beta\in[y,1/4]\\ell(\beta)&\text{if }\beta\in[1/4,1/2]\\r(\beta)&\text{if }\beta\in[1/2,1].\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture seeks the profile of $S_{2,1}$ across edge densities by comparing explicit construction lower bounds with upper bounds from the listed constructions; the exact thresholds and the sharpness of the upper bounds remain open.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Bernard Lidický, Dhruv Mubayi, Florian Pfender and Jan Volec, “Semi-Inducibility of some small graphs”, arXiv:2601.03433 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Carpentier's motif-counting conjecture for community recovery in the stochastic block model
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph with $(v_1,v_2)\notin E$. For any partition of $V$ into $\ell$ groups in which $v_1$ and $v_2$ belong to the same group, let $E^{\neq}$ be the set of edges of $E$ joining distinct groups, and set

$$
r:=\frac{|E|}{|V|-2}.
$$

**Carpentier's motif-counting conjecture.** If

$$
|E^{\neq}|\geq r(\ell-1),
$$

for every such partition, and if $q\asymp n^{-1/r}$ and $\lambda\geq_{\log}q^{1-\log_n(K)}$, then the communities in the stochastic block model can be recovered by an algorithm based on $P_G$, the count of occurrences of the motif $G$.

The conjecture identifies a sufficient combinatorial condition on a motif for counting its occurrences to achieve community recovery in the regime with more than $\sqrt n$ communities. The supplied text does not state whether this claim has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Alexandra Carpentier, Christophe Giraud and Nicolas Verzelen, “Phase Transition for Stochastic Block Model with more than n Communities (II)”, arXiv:2511.21526 (2025).

record.title: Uniform expansion conjecture for quasirandom groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Say that $G$ is **$\varepsilon$-quasirandom** if every non-trivial irreducible complex representation of $G$ has dimension at least $\varepsilon^{-1}$; a Cayley graph of $G$ is **connected** when its generating set generates $G$, and it is an $\varepsilon$-uniform expander** when its expansion constant is bounded below uniformly in the generating set by a quantity depending on $\varepsilon$ only.

**Uniform expansion conjecture.** If $G$ is $\varepsilon$-quasirandom, then all connected Cayley graphs of $G$ are $\varepsilon$-uniform expanders.

This extends Breuillard's conjecture from finite simple groups of Lie type of bounded rank to all quasirandom groups and all generating sets. The source states that the analogous conjecture for bounded-cardinality generating sets is equivalent, via Theorem~, to Breuillard's conjecture; the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Luca Sabatini, “Cayley graphs of quasirandom groups”, arXiv:2606.03801 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03801

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
